idiom_name: plain screen-state struct with methods and explicit re-render callbacks (Fyne data binding where a toolkit exists)
implementation_notes: The model is an ordinary struct with methods: exported fields or getters for the view, methods as commands, and no toolkit import - which already provides the testability half, because a Go test drives the struct directly. What Go does not provide is synchronization: there is no binding mechanism, so the view either re-reads the struct after every command or the model holds callbacks (func() values or a channel) that the view registers. GUI toolkits in Go stay thin; where Fyne is the toolkit, its data binding package (one-way and two-way bindings for widgets) is the closest thing to framework synchronization, with every connection still established by hand. Prefer the framework path when binding whole widgets is worth the dependency; otherwise explicit reload is idiomatic.
pitfalls: Copying the struct copies the state: methods on the pointer receiver mutate the original, but handing the struct to a callback passes a snapshot, so the view keeps rendering stale values.

GUI toolkits (Fyne and the webview-based shells) are not goroutine-safe for widget updates: a state change made on a worker goroutine must be handed back to the UI goroutine (channel or toolkit marshalling) or the frame is corrupted.
There is no weak reference: a callback or subscriber slice registered by a discarded view leaks that view until it is deregistered by hand.
